articleTitle: Reducing power spectrum regrowth for concurrent dual-band OFDM signals
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: Concurrent multi-band or dual-band transmitters and receivers are the key components for future wireless communication. However, the nonlinearity and memory effects caused by power amplifiers will degrade the performance of transmitters and receivers and produce undesired interference to other channels. In this article, the out-of-band intermodulation is discussed, and a method of two-dimensional digital (2D-DPD) is applied to linearize the spectrum for dual-band OFDM signals based on an inverse auto-regression moving-average (IM-ARMA) model.

articleTitle: A learning-based beam training method for multi-user milli-meter wave systems
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we propose a hierarchical learning-based beam selection algorithm for multi-users (MU) in vehicular-to-infrastructure (V2I) milli-metre wave communication systems, which attempts to maximize the sum-rate and reduce the beam training overhead. A graph learning model is developed to achieve the initial beam pair selection, exploring the potential correlation between users. The chosen beam pairs are then fine-tuned through a modified sequential downlink uplink sweeping method (SDU). Compared with the conventional beam training method, simulation results based on ray-tracing channel data confirm that our proposed method remains good sum-rate performance with much reduced training overhead. In the case of 8 users, the proposed method achieves the same sum-rate with the conventional SDU scheme, while the overhead of beam pair training is reduced by a factor of 1.26.

articleTitle: Secure transmission in wireless powered cooperative communication network with finite energy storage
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper investigates secure transmission in a wireless powered cooperative communication network (WPCCN), where multiple intermediate energy harvesting (EH) nodes are deployed to assist the secure transmission between a source and a destination in the presence of an eavesdropper. Each intermediate EH node has a finite energy storage (battery) to accumulate the energy harvested from the source's radio frequency (RF) signal. In order to exploit the intermediate nodes for secure improvement, a relay-and-jammer selection scheme called energy threshold based best-relay and bestjammer (ETBB) is proposed according to the energy storage status and channel gains. Specifically, one node is selected as relay to forward the source's confidential signal, and another node is selected to jam the eavesdropper. Moreover, for evaluating the secrecy performance, the evolution of the EH nodes' energy storage has to be tracked firstly since the residual energy at each EH node is a critical factor that affects the transmit power. Using finite-state Markov Chain (FSMC), we study the long-term energy evolution at the EH nodes. Based on this, we derive the analytical expression for the hybrid outage probability (HOP) of the considered WPCCN. Finally, simulation results reveal that the ETBB scheme outperforms the existing bR-bJ scheme due to the consideration of the energy accumulation issue and the energy storage status at the EH nodes. And, there is a suitable value of the energy threshold for the ETBB scheme to achieve the optimal secrecy performance.

articleTitle: Lowering the error floor of LDPC codes based on bit-rectification strategy
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a bit-rectification strategy to lower error floor of Low-density parity-check codes. Most erroneous bits are located by bit-searching algorithm and obtain more reliable message over parallel concatenated decoder. The negative effect of erroneous bits along with corresponding trapping sets will be avoided.

articleTitle: DocGAN: Document image unwarping for high-level vision task
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: Document digitization is an important means for recording physical painted documents and it helps people to access them anytime, anywhere. With the ubiquitousness of mobile cameras, capturing document images becomes one of the most convenient methods to digitizing a document as well as flatbed scanners. However, there always have some poor conditions when photographing physical documents, which make the acquired images may contain certain degradations such as fold. During our investigation, we notice that although there are plenty of methods trying to unwarping the document images, which may using on mobile applications or other multimedia occasions, few of them focuses on the high-level vision task, for example, text localization and recognition, but only on the image qualitative evaluation, which can not reflect the real repairing quality. Hence, in this paper, we study how methods of document unwarping effect the subsequent high-level text task, and base on that we propose a generative adversarial network to achieve this goal on both image quality and text recognition.

articleTitle: Progressive optimal convolutional network for image compressive sensing reconstruction
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: Wireless multimedia sensor network (WMSN) is a comprehensive network integrating sensors, wireless communication and embedded information processing. However, image, as an important data form in WMSN, will seriously affect the performance of WMSN if it is adopted according to the traditional Nyquist sampling theorem. Recently, deep learning based compressive sensing (CS) methods have made significant improvement in image processing. In the existing methods, the input image is usually measured and reconstructed block by block. Although such block-wise approach can avoid high computational complexity, it can produce obvious block effect in reconstructed images. In this paper, we propose a progressive optimal convolutional network for CS reconstruction (PCSRN), which contains three components: a progressive measurement module (PMM), and a progressive reconstruction module (PRM) followed by a residual reconstruction module (RRM). Specifically, we employ an optimal CS coding network to progressively conduct the CS measurement processing. To further eliminate block effect, the RRM is derived to refine the decoded reconstruction by PRM and obtain the CS reconstruction with high-quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed PCSRN achieves superior performance in terms of quantitative assessment and visual quality.

articleTitle: A cache-based pre-downloading scheme for HSR communication using C-RAN
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: The proliferation of the high-speed railway (HSR) promotes the rapid development of communication technology greatly. In this paper, we explore the application of the cloud radio access network (C-RAN) with the limited-capacity fronthaul in HSR scenarios. Moreover, a cache-based pre-downloading scheme for dynamic resource allocation is proposed to maximize the throughput of the HSR communication system. Specifically, the remote radio heads (RRH) are added with cache devices to store the resources in advance based on the pre-downloading scheme by using the predictable train trajectory information. The simulation result reveals that total network throughput based on the proposed scheme outperforms both the non-cache-based scheme and the conventional cache-based scheme, indicating that the proposed scheme provides some new insights on the enhancement of the HSRs network performance.

articleTitle: An efficient decoding implementation of PCGC with lower error floor
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: Parallel Concatenated Gallager codes usually has error floor phenomenon due to insufficient use of extrinsic information. We propose an effective serial decoding scheme to lower error floor of component LDPC codes through mutual coordination of component decoders. Simulation results show that it outperforms PEG-LDPC codes.

articleTitle: A novel lightweight multimedia network for teacher pose estimation in classroom videos
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: Minor education is a foundation of our country. But now the unbalance of education in different areas causes serious problems. Recently, the usage of artificial intelligence in various fields provides new solutions to some traditional difficulties. With the development of education and artificial intelligence, the relationship between 1+N education and multimedia networks is closer. Intelligent algorithms can extract information that can instruct teaching behavior from educational videos and audios. This paper first analyzes the necessity and meanings of teacher pose estimation in classroom videos. Then a new multimedia network architecture is proposed. The network is fully connected with MobilenetV2 as the backbone. It also uses feature pyramid network for feature fusion. Compared with other algorithms, our new network architecture has obvious advantages in speed. And experiment results prove its advantages in speed and good performances.

articleTitle: Tradeoff between reliability and channel utilization efficiency for 5G NR in unlicensed spectrum
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: With the development of next fifth generation (5G) communication system, unlicensed spectrum has been considered as a central candidate to offload data traffic. In addition to the most important issue of fair coexistence with Wi-Fi, another problem is to reduce the transmission latency in unlicensed band. Grant-free can be used as an important solution to reduce latency by randomly accessing without scheduling, but it brings lower reliability. In this paper, the grant-free uplink transmission with multiple transmission times (GUL-M) is introduced into the coexistence system of Wi-Fi and new radio in unlicensed band (NR-U) to improve transmission reliability by transmitting one data packet several times at the same time. Based on Markov chain model, the performance of coexistence system is analyzed by deriving the transmission probability and collision probability of Wi-Fi and NR-U with GUL-M. Corroborated by simulations, our approach can achieve the tradeoff between reliability and channel utilization efficiency by dynamically adjusting the transmission times, which shows that as the transmission times increases, there is a maximum throughput efficiency for both NR-U with GUL-M and the coexistence system.

articleTitle: Human behavior identification in elevator based on sensor data
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: The paper mainly studies the identification of human behavior in the elevator (straight ladder) based on sensor data collected by external devices. The paper develops an application to obtain sensor. Then preprocess the data, extract features, and build the data set. The paper uses support vector machine, decision tree and random forest algorithm for behavior recognition. The human behavior in the elevator: normal behavior, such as normal standing; lame; hitting the wall of the elevator. Then, the single sensor and multi-sensor feature data sets are respectively used for training. Use the 10-fold cross-validation method to evaluate. Finally, it can be seen from the results that multi-sensor can improve the recognition accuracy. At the same time, the random forest model has the best classification performance: the accuracy is 95%, precision is 95%, recall rate is 95%, and F1-score is 95%, which can achieve very accurate identification.

articleTitle: Fair-energy trajectory plan for multi-target omnidirectional coverage based on cooperative UAVs
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: Owing to flexibility and low cost, omnidirectional coverage on multi-target based on cooperative Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) becomes attractive in surveillance mission recently. Although the camera technology has developed rapidly, it still faces challenges in omnidirectional coverage because of constraints on photographing ability of onboard camera sensors. First, due to inherent errors of camera sensors, the same target has to be covered by different UAVs to avoid large accumulated coverage error. Second, since the routes circling targets are modeled into regular polygons with different number of sides, the numbers of UAVs covering different targets is required to be different. Finally, the flight duration of UAV is limited since the onboard energy has a limitation. In this paper, to complete multi-target omnidirectional coverage mission in fair-energy fashion, we aim at planning trajectories for UAVs to minimize the maximum energy consumption. We propose a two-stage heuristic algorithm, in which we first adjust genetic algorithm to allocate targets to UAVs and then use a greedy algorithm to allocate polygon sides to UAVs. Compared with other algorithms, extensive simulations show that the proposed algorithm can reduce up to 16.2% and 13.2% in terms of maximum and average energy consumption, respectively.

publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: For network transmission, low-dimensional representation of data is powerful compression and computation saving. However, the existing methods fail in further discovering the latent multi-modality characteristic of 3D information. In order to discover the low-dimensional multi-modality features of 3D face shape, in this paper, we present a 3D facial expression recognition method by using the covariance local descriptor and Riemannian kernel sparse coding to make more easily to interact and exchange information. The covariance local descriptor is obtained by fusing multiple features which are extracted around a set of key points on 3D face surface including geometry, deformation and texture information. Due to the nonlinear space of covariance matrix (i.e. symmetric positive define matrix), the Riemannian kernel sparse coding is used to recognize the facial expressions. The experimental results on BU-3DFE database have demonstrated the effectiveness and excellent performance of our method in dealing with easy-confused expression pairs. Meanwhile, the recognition accuracy has a distinguish improvement compare to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Intelligent identification of illegal broadcast based on distributed spectrum monitoring
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: The rapid discovery and recognition of illegal broadcast signals are very important in daily radio management. Speech recognition technology can assist in monitoring and identifying illegal broadcast signals to achieve an intelligent and automated broadcast radio supervision. In this paper, we describe a distributed spectrum monitoring system that can detect and identify illegal broadcast signals in time. This system identifies illegal broadcast signals based on Speech recognition technology. Further, we build a real scene and test the performance of this system. The results show that the speech recognition accuracy rate of the broadcast audio increased by 4.8% through our broadcast audio preprocessing method, and the identification accuracy rate of illegal broadcast reach up to 95%.

articleTitle: Joint offloading strategy and trajectory optimization for aerial-ground cooperative mobile edge computing systems
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have been widely used in wireless communication systems because of their flexibility and maneuverability. In this paper, for more efficient computing services, we consider computing tasks offloading in an air-ground system that a ground base station (GBS) and a UAV cooperatively serve the ground users. Our goal is to minimize the total transmission energy consumptions of the ground users by jointly optimizing the multi-user offloading strategy and the UAV's trajectory, while ensuring UAV's mobility and task delay constraints. This problem includes non-convex objective function, binary variables and non-convex constraints. Therefore, we transform the original problem into two tractable subproblems by introducing the auxiliary variables and relaxing the binary variables. Furthermore, we propose an alternative optimization algorithm to handle these sub-problems. Simulation results illustrate that our proposed algorithm can significantly reduce the total transmission energy consumptions of the ground users.

articleTitle: Navigation with low-sampling-rate GPS and smartphone sensors: A data-driven learning-based approach
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: For vehicle navigation, an inertial navigation system (INS) is often used to assist the global positioning system (GPS); but the positioning accuracy is well known to be sensitive to both the GPS sampling rate and inertial sensor error aggregation. As such, many practical navigation systems adopt both highend INS and high GPS sampling rate, which costs more for hardware on the one hand and demands excessive energy consumption and communications on the other hand. In this work, we propose a learning-based approach that is capable of providing the same level of positioning accuracy but using merely cheap, low-end mobile inertial sensors and integrated GPS with very low sampling rate. The proposed approach consists of a Kalman filter and two multilayer neural networks to realize 3-dimensional, high-precision vehicle navigation. The key to the impressive outcome is the combination of the classic statespace Kalman filter with a new data-driven machine learning mechanism. The proposed approach is evaluated with real trajectory data collected on campus of CUHKSZ, and the results show that it can achieve a positioning error around 8m when the GPS sampling interval is as large as 30s (30 times of nowadays regular sampling interval). Apart from this, the proposed approach also demonstrates good adaptiveness to changing trajectories.

articleTitle: Physical layer security in NOMA-enabled cognitive radio networks
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper investigates physical layer security (PLS) in nonorthogonal multiple access-enabled (NOMA-enabled) cognitive radio networks (CRNs). Considering an existing eavesdropper, the NOMA-enabled CRNs transfer data with the decode-and-forward (DF) collaborative mode over Nakagami-m channels. To analyze the advantages of NOMA-enabled CRNs in PLS perspective, the secrecy performance is evaluated by the closed-form expressions for connection outage probability (COP), secrecy outage probability (SOP) and effective secrecy throughput (EST). In addition, Monte Carlo simulations are provided to verify the derived analytical results and provide insights into the impact of the parameters on the system performance. We analyze the effect of channel parameter m on the secrecy performance and find that at low SNR, the performance in Nakagami-m channels as channel parameter m = 2 is better than that in Rayleigh channels (m = 1). In the end, we demonstrate that secondary users with NOMA scheme can achieve a higher EST than that with orthogonal multiple access (OMA) scheme.

articleTitle: Channel pruning for object detection network
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: With the rapid development of mems technology, wireless communication technology, computing technology and sensor technology, wireless sensor network (WSN), a multidisci-plinary technology integrating information perception, information processing and information transmission, has become a hot research field in the world. As one of the key application fields of wireless sensor network, mobile object detection and tracking has a broad prospect. But the large number of parameters in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) leads to slow speed of object detection, which hinders the application of object detection in mobile devices. Therefore, we propose a method of channel pruning that can reduce the model size of object detection network. Two kinds of pruning schemes for object detection network are adopted, that is, global pruning scheme and local pruning scheme. Our pruning schemes are tested on the traditional receptive field block net (RFBNet). Global pruning scheme can compress the model size to 60% of the original size with only 1.4% loss of mAP under the pruning rate of 0.5. In the local pruning scheme, when only some of the modules in RFBNet are pruned, the model size can be reduced by 35% under the pruning rate of 0.7, and the mAP only reduces by 1%. The experiment demonstrates that our channel pruning method can effectively decrease the size of model.

articleTitle: UAV-enabled MEC system: Locations and coverage optimization
publicationTitle: IET 8th International Conference on Wireless, Mobile & Multimedia Networks
abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC) can significantly enhance the computation capability of mobile devices and reduce their energy consumptions. Compared with terrestrial base stations, UAVs are flexible and easy to deploy, so they can provide more flexible and reliable edge computing services for ground users. In this paper, we study an UAV-enabled MEC system, where the UAV group serves as an edge server group to provide computing offloading services for high-density ground users. Ground users within UAV's coverage will choose local computing or offload to UAVs based on the principle of minimizing the weighted sum of their energy consumption and the delay. In order to serve more ground users and control the growth of its own energy consumption, each UAV will find an appropriate hover point and determine the coverage at a fixed height. We model the problem as a game model, and obtain the Nash equilibrium (NE) point by our Multi-agent Intelligent-learning Algorithm (MIA). Simulation results show that our algorithm has better performance, and each UAV can achieve a balance between the number of ground users it serves and its own energy consumption.
